paragraphs.source_en: Now, like the children’s minimum departure fee, the electrons in a metal must be jostled by a photon posessing a certain minimum energy in order to be kicked off the surface. (As with the children fighting for money, it is extremely unlikely that any one electron gets hit by more than one photon—most don’t get hit at all.) But if the impinging light beam’s frequency is too low, its individual photons wil] lack the punch necessary to eject electrons. Just as no children can afford to leave regardless of the huge total number of coins the adults shower upon them, no electrons are jostled free regardless of the huge total energy embodied in the impinging light beam, if its frequency (and thus the energy of its individual photons) is too low.
